candidates.attacker_control: Archive entry names (`nextEntry.getName()`) from the archive being expanded — for instance an attacker-supplied tar/cpio/zip/7z expanded via Expander.expand(...) or the Archiver/Expander CLI-style helpers.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the guard and the write call in source; canonicalization does block classic '../..' escapes and absolute child names (File(parent, child) treats an absolute child as relative on Unix). Considered that changes.xml claims the sibling-prefix case was already fixed, but the source still uses the un-separated startsWith, and the ExpanderTest referenced by ParameterizedExpanderTest.java line 51 is absent from the snapshot — consistent with this snapshot being the vulnerable revision rather than a fixed one. The issue is not exploitable when archives are trusted or no prefix-sharing writable sibling path exists.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite outside the intended extraction directory, constrained to paths whose canonical form begins with the target directory string (attacker can clobber data/config of adjacent directories named with the target directory's name as a prefix). No full '/etc/...' escape is achievable through this bypass alone.
candidates.prerequisites: Caller uses Expander (or a wrapper) to expand an untrusted archive into a filesystem directory whose canonical path is a string prefix of some other writable path (sibling directory such as 'extract_old', 'extract_backup', or a differently named path sharing the prefix). The process must be able to create/write files in that prefix-sharing location.
candidates.root_cause: Expander.expand(ArchiveEntrySupplier, EntryWriter, File) computes `String targetDirPath = targetDirectory.getCanonicalPath()` and validates each entry with `if (!f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirPath)) throw ...`, where `f = new File(targetDirectory, nextEntry.getName())`. A bare String.startsWith() has no component/separator boundary, so any canonical path that merely begins with the target directory's name (e.g. target '/srv/extract' and entry '../extract_old/x' -> '/srv/extract_old/x') passes the check. The subsequent `parent.mkdirs()` and `Files.newOutputStream(f.toPath())` use the non-normalized File, so the write actually lands in the sibling tree. Plain '../../etc/...' escapes are rejected (canonical path does not share the prefix), so this is the specific prefix-sharing edge case.
candidates.title: Path-traversal bypass in Expander.expand() canonical-path prefix check
candidates.trace: expand(ArchiveEntrySupplier, EntryWriter, File) [line 239] -> supplier.getNextReadableEntry() supplies an entry whose name is controlled by the archive [line 242] -> File f = new File(targetDirectory, nextEntry.getName()) [line 244] -> f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirPath) without a separator boundary returns true for a canonical path that only shares the string prefix [line 245] -> parent.mkdirs() [lines 254-257] and Files.newOutputStream(f.toPath()) [line 258] create/write the file outside targetDirectory.
candidates.unverified: Static source review only; no runtime reproduction, no filesystem/OS-specific verification (Windows/Unix canonicalization and separator behavior), and the exact upstream fix commit was not consulted. The practical exploit scenario depends on the deployment's directory layout satisfying the prefix condition.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

coverage_summary: Model-visible snapshot: 411 files (412 according to scope; 1 sensitive-name/path file excluded, 0 symlinks). P1 index parsed 347 Java files / 5589 symbols / 14165 edges, but is partial: 181 files omitted from the index, semantic resolution and control/data-flow are 'not_implemented', 9712 calls unresolved; index labels were used only for navigation and every cited location was re-read in source. I read in depth: archivers/examples (Expander, Archiver), changes.xml, security-reports.xml, and substantial parts of archivers/zip (ZipArchiveInputStream, NioZipEncoding). I did not deeply audit sevenz, tar, cpio, arj, dump, bzip2/lzma/lz4/snappy compressor codecs, ChangeSetPerformer, IOUtils/ByteUtils, or the test suite beyond targeted searches.
limitations: Relation index coverage is partial (181 files omitted, 9712 unresolved calls, no data-flow/control-flow, no semantic resolution); unreported areas were not reviewed merely because the index has no record there.
No code was executed; no tests, scanners, or builds were run, so the finding is a static lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.
Binary files and a sensitive-name/path file were skipped by the tooling; hidden VCS metadata was not available to confirm the exact upstream commit/date.
The Expander finding depends on deployment layout (a writable path whose canonical form begins with the target directory string), which could not be validated at runtime.
The NioZipEncoding DoS lead and any zip EOF/large-allocation issues were not fully traced to an exploitable entry point.

rejected_leads.lead: NioZipEncoding.encode() can loop forever on a file name ending with an unpaired high surrogate: the loop calls enc.encode(cb, out, false) and has no UNDERFLOW branch, so a dangling surrogate leaves cb.remaining()>0 while the encoder repeatedly returns UNDERFLOW (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/NioZipEncoding.java lines 85-116). This matches the description of CVE-2019-12402 (infinite loop in the file-name encoding algorithm when writing archives).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible DoS and source-level bug, but left unconfirmed: requires a String containing a dangling surrogate in an entry name, the snapshot carries no changelog/CVE entry for it, and the dataset mapping/timing for VUL4J-5 could not be verified without external patch information.

rejected_leads.lead: ZipArchiveInputStream read()/readStored()/readDeflated() EOF and unknown-size handling (possibly CVE-2018-11771-style infinite reads).
rejected_leads.reason: Inspected read paths (lines 428-587) and found no concrete mis-return of EOF that could be confirmed from source alone; the COMPRESS-454 stored-entry/data-descriptor fix is already present and current code closely matches later upstream structure. Insufficient evidence.

summary: Apache Commons Compress 1.18-SNAPSHOT (post-1.17). Reviewed the archive-writing/extraction helpers and the zip core with the P1 relation index as navigation only. Strongest source-supported issue: the `Expander` example/API class (shipped in the main artifact) guards extraction with a raw canonical-string prefix test that lacks a path-separator boundary, so entries whose canonical path shares the target directory's name as a string prefix are written outside the intended target directory. The repository's own changelog (changes.xml) describes exactly this sibling-prefix edge case as a path-traversal bug, while the guard in Expander.java still does not contain the boundary check, and the changelog-referenced `ExpanderTest` is absent from the snapshot — consistent with a vulnerable revision. A second plausible DoS lead (NioZipEncoding infinite loop on a name ending in an unpaired surrogate) is recorded as an unconfirmed rejected lead rather than a second candidate.
